rows.basis: Cloud Memory Business Unit revenue (hyperscale cloud memory and all HBM), recast for the year the segment was created. CDBU's 2.124bn is excluded because it includes enterprise storage and non-AI DRAM. CMBU in fiscal 2023 is mostly pre-HBM-ramp cloud memory, so it overstates AI. No total revenue value is in the pack, so no share is given.

CMBU revenue, the cloud and HBM line, recast to the fiscal 2025 segments. CDBU's 4.984bn is excluded; the releases say only in words that AI drove data center and HBM growth. No total revenue value is in the pack.

CMBU revenue, which the MD&A says rose 257% on AI demand for HBM, high-capacity DIMMs and LP server DRAM. CDBU's 7.229bn is excluded, and the stated 'data center >50%' is a quarterly data-center share, not an AI share. No total revenue value is in the pack.

CMBU revenue, the cloud and HBM line. CDBU's 37.592bn is excluded; the 10-K's ~60% data-center share is not an AI share, and there is no HBM revenue figure. The FY2026-tagged MD&A quotes (+257%/+45%) match the FY2025 text, not FY2026's segment growth.

Micron said it is making 'disciplined investments ... to satisfy growing AI-driven memory demand' but gave no HBM or AI share of the 15.857bn capex. The seller-side signal is the 13.524bn of CMBU revenue.
The May 2025 release frames fiscal 2025 investment as meant to 'satisfy growing AI-driven memory demand', with no amount or share.

Micron is 'investing in our global manufacturing footprint to support' customers' AI-era memory demand. It states no HBM or AI share of the 30.712bn gross capex, so the total is the whole, not the AI part. The seller-side signal is the 43.085bn of CMBU revenue.
